name: payroll
description: Employees, timesheets with weekly overtime, progressive income tax and deductions in Decimal, payslips and a monthly payroll report.
author: test2 benchmark author

issues.description: The docstring (and README) say half a cent rounds up, but quantize without a rounding mode uses the context default ROUND_HALF_EVEN, so 2.345 becomes 2.34.
prorate takes (amount, part, whole) but is called with the month length as the part and the days employed as the whole, so a mid-month joiner is paid more than the full salary.
When a new department starts only the headcount is reset; gross, deductions and net keep the previous departments' sums, so every department after the first includes the ones before it.
issues.fix_hint: Reset gross, deductions and net to ZERO together with headcount when the department changes.

issues.description: The department typed into the HR web form is formatted into the SQL text, so a value like "x' OR '1'='1" returns every employee (or runs other SQL).
issues.fix_hint: Use a ? placeholder and pass (department,) as the parameters.

issues.description: The overtime rule (hours above 40 per ISO week) is implemented again in the report with its own WEEKLY_HOURS constant instead of using timesheets.split_overtime and OVERTIME_THRESHOLD; a change to the rule in one place leaves the report disagreeing with the payslips.
About 60 lines that validate the input and render four separate sections (employees, departments, totals, overtime) plus a zero-pay note; each section should be its own helper.
_payslip_block is a line-for-line copy of Payslip.render_text; the report should reuse the payslip's own rendering.

decoys.anchor: query = f"SELECT * FROM employees WHERE employee_id IN ({placeholders})"
decoys.why_it_is_fine: The f-string only inserts a run of '?' placeholders; the ids themselves are passed as query parameters.
MD5 is the checksum format the bank's upload form asks for, used only to detect damaged uploads, not for security (and marked usedforsecurity=False).
